# Nextdoor Pet Business Marketing: The Local Channel Guide

For a **Nextdoor pet business**, the platform is one of the cheapest and highest-trust local marketing channels available: a free Business Page lets verified neighbors recommend you, and those recommendations surface every time someone in your area asks “Who’s a good groomer?” or “Any daycare you trust?” Pet services are among the most requested topics in neighborhood feeds, and the audience is exactly who you want: nearby homeowners and renters with pets, often ready to book this week. The playbook is simple: claim your page, collect recommendations from happy clients, reply helpfully (not salesy) when neighbors ask, and make booking effortless once they click through.

## Why is Nextdoor so underrated for pet businesses?

Most owners pour effort into Instagram and Google, then ignore Nextdoor. That’s a mistake for three reasons:

*   **Hyper-local reach.** Members are verified to a neighborhood, so your audience is people who live minutes from your salon, daycare, or mobile route, not followers across the country.
*   **Word of mouth, at scale.** Pet owners choose groomers and daycares largely on personal referrals. Nextdoor turns a private referral into a public, searchable one that keeps working for months.
*   **High intent.** A neighbor posting “Need a groomer for my doodle, who do you love?” is already shopping. Few channels put you in front of buyers that close to a decision.

It also costs nothing to start. The core tools, a Business Page, recommendations, and posting updates, are free.

## How do you set up a Nextdoor pet business page?

Plan on about 30 minutes to do it well:

1.  **Claim or create your page.** Search for your business first; a neighbor may have already mentioned you, creating a page you can claim.
2.  **Choose accurate categories** such as pet grooming, dog daycare, pet boarding, or pet store, so you appear in the right searches.
3.  **Complete every field:** address or service area (mobile groomers should list the neighborhoods they cover), hours, phone, and website.
4.  **Add real photos:** your space, your team, and finished pets (with owner permission). Authentic beats polished.
5.  **Write a plain-language description:** services, breeds or sizes you specialize in, and what makes you different, such as “Fear Free certified” or “cage-free drying.”
6.  **Link directly to online booking** so a curious neighbor can go from recommendation to appointment in one tap.

## How do you get more Nextdoor recommendations?

Recommendations are the engine. They show up on your page, in search, and in replies when neighbors ask for suggestions. Aim for a steady trickle, not a one-time burst.

*   **Ask at the right moment:** at checkout when a client is thrilled with a fresh groom, or when a daycare parent comments on how tired and happy their dog is.
*   **Make it easy:** put a QR code linking to your page at the front desk and include the link in your post-visit thank-you text or email.
*   **Target your regulars first.** Loyal clients and members are most willing to vouch for you publicly.
*   **Thank every recommender** publicly and personally. It encourages others and builds goodwill.

> On Nextdoor, your best salesperson isn’t you. It’s the neighbor whose dog you groomed last Tuesday.

### What about Neighborhood Faves?

Nextdoor periodically recognizes locally loved businesses based on recommendations. Earning that badge is a useful credibility signal to display in your shop and on social media, and the only real strategy is consistently earning recommendations.

## What should a pet business post on Nextdoor?

Neighbors tolerate helpful local content and tune out ads. Post from your Business Page roughly once or twice a week and follow Nextdoor’s community guidelines. Ideas that perform well:

*   **Seasonal safety tips:** hot-pavement warnings in summer, holiday food hazards, fireworks anxiety, winter paw care.
*   **Lost-pet help:** offer to share lost-dog posts or scan found pets for microchips if you have a scanner.
*   **Community events:** adoption days with a local rescue, a free nail-trim clinic, or a pet photo day.
*   **Genuine availability:** “We just added Saturday openings for large breeds” is useful news, not spam.
*   **Behind the scenes:** meet the new groomer, a before-and-after of a matted rescue (with permission).

### How should you respond when neighbors ask for recommendations?

Let clients recommend you first when possible. If you reply yourself, be transparent that you’re the owner, answer the actual question (price range, breed experience, availability), and skip hard-sell language. A helpful, honest reply earns trust from everyone reading the thread, not just the person who asked.

## How does Nextdoor compare with other local channels?

| Channel | Cost to start | Main strength | Main limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nextdoor | Free (paid ads optional) | Verified neighbors, high-trust recommendations | Smaller audience; community-first rules on promotion |
| Google Business Profile | Free | Captures “groomer near me” searches and maps | Competitive; reviews take time to build |
| Instagram / Facebook | Free (paid ads optional) | Visual storytelling, before-and-after photos | Reach is broad, not necessarily local |
| Email and SMS to clients | Low | Rebooking and retention of existing clients | Doesn’t reach new customers on its own |

Nextdoor works best alongside these channels: it brings in new neighbors, Google confirms your reputation, and email and SMS keep those new clients coming back.

## Is paid advertising on Nextdoor worth it for a pet business?

Nextdoor offers paid options, including self-serve ads and local deals targeted to nearby neighborhoods. They can work for a launch, a new location, or a daycare with open capacity. Start small, a modest monthly budget for a single clear offer such as “first groom 20% off,” and track results with a dedicated promo code so you know what each booking cost. Build your free recommendations first; ads convert far better when your page already shows neighbor trust.

## How do you turn Nextdoor attention into booked appointments?

Local buzz is wasted if booking is hard. The winning setup:

*   **Online booking** linked from your Business Page, so neighbors can book at 10 p.m. without calling.
*   **A trackable offer** (a code like NEXTDOOR15) so you can measure new clients from the channel.
*   **Automated reminders and rebooking prompts** so a first visit becomes a regular schedule.
*   **Packages or memberships** that give new clients a reason to commit.

# 8 Essential Dog Grooming Marketing Strategies

By [Hibu](https://hibu.com/blog/authors/hibu) | January 14, 2025

*   [facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fhibu.com%2Fblog%2Findustries%2F8-essential-dog-grooming-marketing-strategies&src=sdkpreparse)

*   [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=false&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhibu.com%2Fblog%2Findustries%2F8-essential-dog-grooming-marketing-strategies)
*   [Linkedin](mailto:?subject=8%20Essential%20Dog%20Grooming%20Marketing%20Strategies&body=https%3A%2F%2Fhibu.com%2Fblog%2Findustries%2F8-essential-dog-grooming-marketing-strategies)

As the owner of a local dog grooming business, you know how important pets are to their people, and the numbers support this. [According to a 2023 Pew Research Center survey, 97% of US households view pets as family members.](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/industry/pet-grooming-boarding/1735/) This means keeping them happy, healthy, and looking great is often a top priority. Of course, that’s where you and your business come in.

Currently, [the global pet grooming market is worth over $1.3 billion a year](https://www.dogster.com/lifestyle/pet-grooming-industry-statistics), and it’s only expected to grow. With the rise in pet humanization, an increase in busy lifestyles, and the growth of multi-pet households, pet owners have become more and more willing to pay top prices for the best pet care—and, when they’re searching for that best-in-class care, you want them to choose your business specifically to spend their money.

But how do you do that?

**It all comes down to how you market your services**. We can assume that your expertise is in dog _grooming_, not dog _grooming marketing_. So, we’re more than happy to step in on that front–starting with these eight essential dog grooming marketing strategies that you need to know for your local grooming business.

###   
Eight Dog Grooming Marketing Strategies

The right marketing strategies will ensure that pet owners in your local area will be able to find your business and then book your services. The eight we’ll cover here are the most essential ones, so you’ll want to focus on them first.

#### 1\. Optimize your Google listing

Your Google Business listing helps customers in your area find your business when they search for things like “dog grooming near me.” Keeping your profile optimized is crucial for driving traffic to your business. Keep these tips in mind:

*   **Complete your listing:** ensure your address, phone number, email, website, and any other relevant fields are complete and accurate. 
*   **Add photos**: take high-quality photos of the inside and outside of your business, before and after client photos that showcase your skills, and maybe even shots of yourself to add to your profile.
*    **Respond to reviews:** reviews left on Google will appear on your profile and be visible to other potential customers. Whether the reviews are good or bad, you should always take the time to leave at least a quick response.
*   **Keep your profile up to date:** things change, and holidays may affect your hours. When that happens, keep your customers informed by updating your profile. Make sure to also switch out your photos periodically to keep things fresh.   
     

#### 2\. Continually groom your website

Your website is like your business’s digital first impression. You want to make sure it is optimized for mobile, loads quickly, and is free from any mistakes. Similarly to your Google Business Profile, you’ll want to keep it updated with current photos, business hours, and contact information.

Since you run a service business, you’ll also want to include an online booking portal on your site. [Research shows that 90% of customers prefer booking appointments online, and 35% prefer scheduling them during non-business hours](https://calendesk.com/blog/12-reasons-why-you-need-an-online-booking-system-for-small-business). This feature offers convenience for your current customers and prospects and keeps you competitive in the market.

**\[Related:** [5 Things Customers Want to See on Your Local Business Website](https://hibu.com/blog/marketing-tips/5-things-customers-want-to-see-on-your-local-business-website)**\]**

#### 3\. Create grooming packages

Remember how we mentioned that people were living busier lifestyles? That’s where our next strategy comes in. Create pre-made grooming packages to list (with prices!) on your newly polished website. A menu detailing which services their pet will receive will make the booking process much faster and simpler. Plus, you’re the groomer. You know best which services pets need most and which complement each other best.

If you want, you can still create an “a la carte” menu for those customers who only want to purchase one or two of your services. This could even make your packages more desirable if you indicate the discount customers will receive by purchasing the package instead of each service individually.

#### 4\. Set up a customer referral program

Because pet owners love their pets so much, they aren’t always willing to try out new care providers. That is unless the providers come highly recommended by other pet owners. So, encourage your satisfied customers to tell their friends about you with a customer referral program.

A referral program pulls double duty for you. Not only does it help with brand awareness for your business, but it also rewards your loyal customers. [Studies show that customer acquisitions through referrals spend 200% more than the average customer](https://www.annexcloud.com/blog/42-referral-marketing-statistics-that-will-make-you-want-to-start-a-raf-program-tomorrow/).

From discounts on services for every customer referred to free gifts, the possibilities for how to reward your referrals are endless.

#### 5\. Ask for reviews

In the same vein as customer referrals, reviews are essential for dog grooming businesses. Just as people turn to their friends to discover safe places to care for their pets, they also head to the internet. When they do, you’ll want to ensure your reviews put you ahead of the competition.

Encourage satisfied customers to leave reviews by posting QR codes in your waiting room, emailing them a request after their appointment, or sending a follow-up text message.

# 10 Proven Ways to Attract More Pet Owners to Your Grooming Business

*   June 04, 2026
*   By UPrinting

To attract local customers, pet businesses need to be both visible and trusted. While great service keeps people coming back, it’s important to promote your business so your community remembers you. According to the National Library of Medicine, [41% of dog owners groom their pets at home](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8907591/), 30% use full-service grooming salons, and 9% choose mobile groomers. With so many choices available, strong local marketing is essential if you want your business to stand out. Here are 10 practical tips to help pet businesses get noticed, connect with local customers, and promote their services.

## Quick Guide: Local Marketing Tactics for Pet Groomers

| Goals | Useful Marketing Tool | Why It Works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reach dog owners within the area | Door hangers | Visible signs that target neighborhoods where local pet owners live. |
| Promote seasonal offers | Flyers | A must-have if you want to actively spread your services through events and partner locations. |
| Increase walk-ins | Posters | Placing posters in the area keeps your business visible throughout the community. |
| Get repeat appointments | Reminder cards and loyalty cards | Encourage your customers to schedule their next visit by offering benefits. |
| Build trust locally | Community event materials | Thoughtful event promotions create personal connections with local pet owners. |

## 1\. Door Hangers Help Reach Nearby Pet Owners Fast

If your grooming shop relies on local customers, being seen in your neighborhood is more important than trying to reach the whole city. 

[Door hangers](https://www.uprinting.com/door-hanger.html) work well because they put your business right in front of people who live near your shop. The main thing is to focus on the right areas instead of handing out thousands at random. 

Look for pet-friendly apartment buildings, neighborhoods with walking trails, suburban areas with fenced yards, and places near dog parks or vet clinics where pet owners spend time. 

Keep your door hanger simple and clear. Include one main offer, a strong call to action, your phone number, a QR code for booking, and photos of real pets you’ve groomed if you can. A catchy headline grabs more attention than listing all your services. 

Instead of this: 

“Full-Service Pet Grooming”  

Try using: 

**“Tired of Dog Hair All Over Your Couch?”**  

This speaks directly to a problem many pet owners have. 

## 2\. Build Local Partnerships That Bring Consistent Referrals

Many pet owners tend to trust the first business they come across, whether it's a vet clinic, daycare, or pet supply shop. 

This is why many businesses choose local partnerships over big advertising campaigns. Rather than just using social media, try putting up flyers or small posters where pet owners already go. You can also team up with other pet businesses for cross-promotions, so their customers learn about your services too. 

[Flyers](https://www.uprinting.com/flyer-printing.html) work best when they highlight a specific need, like puppy grooming, flea-season cleanups, shedding treatments, or holiday grooming before family events and photos. 

## 3\. Attractive Posters Can Increase Local Awareness Around Your Shop

[Posters](https://www.uprinting.com/custom-posters.html) are a simple way to get your business noticed in your local area. Most grooming customers don’t book right after seeing your business for the first time. Seeing your shop more than once helps them remember you when they need an appointment. 

Door hangers help you connect directly with people, and flyers are good for referrals and partnerships. Posters, on the other hand, should share useful information and catch people’s attention wherever they are. 

Make sure your poster highlights one problem, offers one clear solution, and gives one easy next step. This way, pet owners will quickly get your message and know what to do. 

For example: 

**“Muddy Dog After the Park? Book a Cleanup Groom Today.”**

This kind of message is more helpful than generic ads. Use big, easy-to-read text, since most people only look at posters for a few seconds. 

## 4\. Create Seasonal Promotions Pet Owners Actually Need

Seasonal offers are a great way to promote your products and services, especially when you connect them to the weather. Pet owners usually respond better when these promotions address the real challenges they face each season. 

Here are some examples: 

*   **Spring:** In spring, pets tend to shed more. This is a good time to promote deshedding services using flyers and posters in your local area. 
*   **Summer:** As the weather gets hotter, many people want shorter grooming styles and treatments that help with odor control. 
*   **Fall:** When school starts again, family routines often change. This makes it a great time to suggest regular grooming appointments.
